end.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 1. Equatorial Regions
end.title: The Equatorial Region: Human Activities (Farming, Lumbering, Hunting and Others)
end.coverNote: Good morning, class. Today we study the human activities of the Equatorial Region: farming, lumbering, hunting and gathering
end.notions: Shifting cultivation, food crop, cash crop, plantation, lumbering, hunting, gathering.
end.focus: Human activities of the Equatorial region: forestry, farming, hunting, lumbering and others (progression sheet, week 5).
end.competence: Learners are able to describe the main activities of people in the Equatorial region and relate them to the forest environment.
objectives: Describe shifting cultivation and plantation agriculture.
Describe hunting, gathering and other activities.
recall: The Equatorial region has timber, water, minerals, wildlife and farmland.
Cocoa, coffee, oil palm and rubber grow well there.
Timber is carried by lorries to the ports.
end.recallNote: Check the homework on food crops and cash crops from the forest region.
end.justification: This lesson helps us to understand how people earn a living in the Equatorial region.
end.homework: Write two problems that forestry, farming or hunting cause to the forest, its animals or its rivers.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 1 (week 7): problems faced, problems caused and attempted solutions.
